title: Maintaining Correct Drain Pipe Slope
description: Maintaining proper drain pipe pitch is critical for long-term wastewater flow and system hygiene. If a pipe lacks sufficient slope, water moves too slowly, leaving solid waste and debris behind to accumulate into stubborn clogs. Conversely, an overly steep slope can allow liquids to rush past solids, leaving debris stranded inside the pipe. Regular maintenance includes verifying pipe alignment and hanger support along exposed basement runs or crawlspaces to prevent sagging, known as pipe bellies. Keeping drain lines steadily sloped according to local plumbing codes ensures liquids and solids travel together effectively.

Maintaining Correct Drain Pipe Slope

Maintaining proper drain pipe pitch is critical for long-term wastewater flow and system hygiene. If a pipe lacks sufficient slope, water moves too slowly, leaving solid waste and debris behind to accumulate into stubborn clogs. Conversely, an overly steep slope can allow liquids to rush past solids, leaving debris stranded inside the pipe. Regular maintenance includes verifying pipe alignment and hanger support along exposed basement runs or crawlspaces to prevent sagging, known as pipe bellies. Keeping drain lines steadily sloped according to local plumbing codes ensures liquids and solids travel together effectively.
